subject: Group differences in one factor but not a second in a multi-group model

messages.author: 80c425a48fb0614e
messages.subject: Group differences in one factor but not a second in a multi-group model
parts:
Hello, 

I have a two-factor CFA and am running a multigroup model. Partial scalar invariance has been established and I want to test the equivalence of one of the two latent means across the two groups. Intuitively, I would use
group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "means"),
group.partial=c("a ~ 1", "latent1 ~1")
as arguments to the cfa() function.

However, this does not seem to work. Latent variables are standardized, so I also use std.lv=T as an argument.

Thanks for the hint, best regards,
Andrea

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Group differences in one factor but not a second in a multi-group model
parts:
Hi, Andrea.

When you set std.lv=TRUE, you force the latent mean to be 0 in all groups.
Either you change std.lv=FALSE or you manually standardize the latent variables manually in your syntax.

I believe the second option would be something like this:

latent1~c(0,NA)*1 #set mean of group 1 to zero and estimate the mean of group 2 latent1~~c(1,1)*latent1 #set latent variance of both groups to 1. If you want to test homocedasticity later, change the second parameter to NA

Best,
Yago

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Re: Group differences in one factor but not a second in a multi-group model
parts:
Hi Andrea,

You can also just use the argument group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"). The latent mean in one group should be automatically set to 0 (on the latent scale, an arbitrary value, think of it as centered variable), and in the other group(s) the latent mean should then be freely estimated. If these values are statistically significantly different from 0, then they are different from the mean in the first group.

Best,
Jošt
